attribution: Polling data via VoteHub (https://votehub.com/polls/api/), licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Retrieved and reshaped by PULSE INTEL — filtered, deduplicated, and reparsed from VoteHub's raw /polls response; this is a modified excerpt, not the original dataset.
methodology: A race is covered only with >=3 distinct polls, fielded in 2026, deduplicated by pollster+start_date+end_date+population, each with sample_size >= 300 and both principal general-election nominees resolved via an exact full-name match first, falling back to an unambiguous exact-last-name match only for a candidate the exact pass did not already resolve (see parse_shares). Where the same candidate's exact name appears more than once in one poll with DIFFERING values, nothing is picked between them (not even the max) — the whole poll is dropped and every value is logged in duplicateAnswerLog, so a systematic bias toward either side is checkable and structurally cannot arise from this script. No pollster grade or rating is available from VoteHub on any endpoint; every poll below carries gradeAvailable: false and grade-weighting must not run against this data until a rating source is added.
